stories.title: Pakistani Minister Visits New Delhi for SCO Cultural Dialogue Forum
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for Climate Change Dr Musadik Malik arrived in New Delhi on Friday to lead Pakistan's delegation at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum. Received by Pakistan's Chargé d'Affaires upon arrival, Malik is attending the event at the invitation of India's Minister of Culture and Tourism to discuss shared heritage, cultural ties, and regional cooperation among member states.

This visit marks the first trip to India by a Pakistani federal minister since May 2023, when then foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari visited Goa for an SCO foreign ministers meeting. The current dialogue takes place against a backdrop of diplomatic strain between Pakistan and India, which have remained in a stalemate following a military confrontation in May 2025 and a deadly incident in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir.

During the forum, Malik will present Pakistan's perspective on the importance of inter-civilisational dialogue and highlight the country's constructive role within the SCO. The Pakistani delegation is scheduled to participate in thematic sessions and interact with representatives from other member states on the sidelines of the event.

Pakistan is currently chairing the SCO Council of Heads of State for the 2026-27 period, a role in which it will host various ministerial and expert group meetings ahead of the upcoming summit. The Foreign Office noted that participation in the forum reflects Islamabad's ongoing commitment to promoting regional understanding under the Shanghai Spirit.

stories.title: Field Marshal Munir Visits North Waziristan to Reaffirm Counterterrorism Resolve
stories.summary:
Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir traveled to Miran Shah in North Waziristan to review the local security situation. During the visit, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations, he received a detailed briefing regarding intelligence-based operations and strategies aimed at securing lasting stability in the region.

Upon arriving, CDF Munir was greeted by the Corps Commander Peshawar. He placed a floral wreath at Yadgar-e-Shuhada to honor the military's fallen personnel and met with troops and officers to evaluate their operational readiness and dedication to national defense.

The army chief also praised the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police, calling them a resilient frontline unit for their sacrifices in combating terrorism and Fitna-al Khwarij. He reiterated the commitment of security forces and law enforcement agencies to eradicate terrorism and protect the peace of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Pakistan has experienced an escalation in violence since 2021, particularly following the Afghan Taliban's return to power. A report by the Centre for Research and Security Studies noted that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan accounted for roughly 96 percent of violence-related fatalities in the second quarter of 2026, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa experiencing the highest share of deaths and violent incidents.

stories.title: Copper Slumps Toward Record Weekly Drop Amid AI Slump and Stronger Dollar
stories.summary:
Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange fell 1.7 percent to $12,310.50 per metric ton by 1030 GMT on Friday, reaching its lowest level since March. The industrial metal, widely utilized in AI infrastructure development, was on track for its steepest weekly decline in over 19 months, dropping approximately 8.2 percent for the week. Analysts noted that investor interest in the artificial intelligence sector is fading while concerns grow regarding aggressive Federal Reserve inflation policies and a strengthening US dollar.

Despite the broader sell-off, Anthropic shares experienced a 6 percent premarket drop following a strong market debut on Thursday, contributing to the persistent downward trend across AI-related equities. Physical markets showed mixed indicators, as China experienced slight relief from previous tightness with import premiums hitting record highs. Shanghai Futures Exchange copper inventories increased by 3,204 tons over the week to reach 30,846 tons, which remains under a single day of Chinese consumption.

Additional physical movements included a rare delivery of 3,850 tons of copper into London Metal Exchange warehouses located in Mobile, Alabama. Meanwhile, the aluminum market faced acute supply pressures, with cash contract premiums over the three-month forward reaching a historic high of $323.50 per ton. Data from the exchange revealed that a single entity maintains control over 30 to 39 percent of all aluminum warrants.

Other base metals also suffered losses during the session, with aluminum declining 0.4 percent to $2,858 per ton and zinc dropping 1.4 percent to $3,517. Lead decreased by 0.4 percent to $1,858.50, nickel fell 0.6 percent to $15,485, and tin decreased by 1.8 percent to $41,105, marking its lowest price point since January 2.

stories.title: Service Retail Explores Acquisition of Pakistan Clothing Chain for Expansion
stories.summary:
Service Retail (Private) Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Service Industries Limited, is currently investigating the potential acquisition of a clothing retail chain in Pakistan. The parent company announced this strategic exploration in an official notice submitted to the Pakistan Stock Exchange on Friday to broaden its domestic operational footprint.

According to the corporate disclosure, any eventual transaction will depend strictly on comprehensive due diligence, necessary regulatory approvals, and the finalization of a binding agreement. The company did not disclose specific details regarding the identity of the targeted business or the financial value of the prospective transaction.

Service Industries Limited was originally incorporated within Pakistan as a private limited entity in 1957 before transitioning into a public limited company. The firm's core business activities encompass the manufacturing, purchasing, and retail sale of footwear, automotive tyres, tubes, and technical rubber products, with substantial export revenue originating primarily from Europe alongside expanding markets in the United States, Australia, and the Middle East.

In 2024, the corporation executed a structural demerger scheme that transferred its tyre division, retail division, and Speed (Private) Limited shares directly to wholly-owned subsidiaries. Following this corporate restructuring, Service Industries Limited functions as a holding company overseeing a diversified commercial portfolio across multiple sectors.

stories.title: US Panel Accuses India of Targeting Minorities in Massive Voter List Revision
stories.summary:
The United States Commission on International Religious Freedom stated on Thursday that India has intensified its targeting of religious minorities during a voter list revision that removed 130 million names nationwide. Asif Mahmood, chair of the bipartisan US panel, accused the Indian government of removing Muslim citizens from voter rolls, labeling them as foreigners, and executing illegal deportations. The mass omission represents the largest voter deletion in the nation's history, with data indicating that the cuts disproportionately affect Muslims, who form India's largest minority population.

India's Election Commission defended the process by stating that the revisions aimed to eliminate duplicate, deceased, shifted, and ineligible voters, while adding that individuals excluded by mistake can pursue official appeals. Conversely, the voter roll update has intersected with separate initiatives to identify suspected illegal immigrants, drawing sharp criticism from international rights experts and domestic opposition parties. Commissioner Gene Mills urged the US State Department to formally designate India as a country of particular concern, though Washington has not acted on previous panel recommendations.

India's Ministry of External Affairs strongly rejected the findings, dismissing the US commission as a prejudiced organization with a political agenda that interferes in internal national affairs. Randhir Jaiswal, the ministry's spokesperson, stated during a Friday media briefing that the body does not warrant serious attention. Recent voter roll updates have also triggered street protests and demonstrations by opposition groups and students, which faced a government crackdown that drew condemnation from rights organizations.

International observers, including United Nations experts and human rights advocates, maintain that hostility toward religious minorities has escalated since Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party took power in 2014. Critics point to rising hate speech, controversial citizenship legislation, property demolitions, and the revocation of Kashmir's autonomy. Meanwhile, the Indian government consistently denies allegations of systemic discrimination, asserting that its national policies and social welfare initiatives provide broad benefits across all communities.

stories.title: Aiden Markram to Captain South Africa in Second Test Against Bangladesh
stories.summary:
Cricket South Africa confirmed that injured captain Temba Bavuma will miss Monday's second Test match against Bangladesh in Centurion due to an ongoing calf injury. Spinning all-rounder Senuran Muthusamy has been added to the squad as a replacement, while Aiden Markram will step in to captain the side. Batter Tony de Zorzi is expected to enter the starting playing eleven in place of Bavuma. South Africa won the opening Test by nine wickets and must secure another victory to preserve their qualification prospects for a consecutive World Test Championship final, having claimed last year's title against Australia.

In addition to the Test squad, Cricket South Africa announced the roster for the upcoming three-match one-day international series against Bangladesh scheduled between December 1 and December 7. Bavuma was also omitted from the ODI lineup, with Keshav Maharaj assigned to captain the team. The ODI squad features recalls for fast bowler Lungi Ngidi, recovering from a hamstring injury, and wicketkeeper-batter Sinethemba Qeshile, who previously played his only two ODIs in Pakistan in November 2025. Young batters Dewald Brevis and Lhuan-dre Pretorius were likewise selected for the fifty-over fixtures.

Sinethemba Qeshile has additionally been named in the squad for the subsequent three-match Twenty20 series, which will take place from December 10 to December 13. Spinner Bjorn Fortuin will serve as captain for the T20 matches. The announced ODI squad features Keshav Maharaj, Dewald Brevis, Corbin Bosch, Gerald Coetzee, Quinton de Kock, Tony de Zorzi, Bjorn Fortuin, Jordan Hermann, Duan Jansen, Nqobani Mokoena, Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Anrich Nortje, Lungi Ngidi, Sinethemba Qeshile, and Tristan Stubbs.

The T20 squad consists of Bjorn Fortuin, Dewald Brevis, Gerald Coetzee, Connor Esterhuizen, Donovan Ferreira, Jordan Hermann, Duan Jansen, Kwena Maphaka, Nqobani Mokoena, Nqaba Peter, Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Sinethemba Qeshile, Tristan Stubbs, and Prenelan Subrayen. The series aims to test emerging talent alongside seasoned international players across both limited-overs formats.

stories.title: Arsenal Defender William Saliba Returns From Injury While Bukayo Saka Stays Out
stories.summary:
Premier League leaders Arsenal are set to welcome back central defender William Saliba for their upcoming fixture against Newcastle. Saliba has been sidelined since July due to a back injury sustained during France's World Cup semi-final defeat against Spain. Manager Mikel Arteta stated that the 25-year-old player is in good physical condition and ready for selection following two recent practice matches. 

However, the team will continue to miss England winger Bukayo Saka, who is expected to remain out of action for another month. Saka sustained a thigh injury during a 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich on October 21. Additionally, midfielder Martin Zubimendi will be unavailable for a few weeks after picking up a hamstring injury while playing for Spain in a Nations League match against England.

Despite these roster challenges, defending champions Arsenal currently sit at the top of the Premier League standings with a five-point lead over second-placed Brighton. The team has secured nine victories out of their first 10 matches, a performance that Arteta attributes to the squad's consistency, quality, and strong desire to win.

In other club developments, Arteta mentioned that Arsenal is nearing an agreement on a new contract with England midfielder Declan Rice, whose current deal runs until 2028. The manager also shared words of support for former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino as he takes over as the manager of Manchester United ahead of a match against Liverpool.

stories.title: Pakistani Rupee Edges Up Slightly Against US Dollar in Inter-Bank Market
stories.summary:
The Pakistani rupee registered a marginal increase against the US dollar in the inter-bank market, closing at 276.51. This marked a slight gain of Re0.01 compared to the previous day's close of 276.52.

On the global front, the US dollar remained close to a 19-month high, driven by a safe-haven rush among investors amid ongoing volatility in the artificial intelligence sector. The dollar index stayed near 103.9, its highest level since early April 2025, supported by hotter-than-expected US inflation data from November 10 that heightened expectations of further policy tightening by the Federal Reserve.

Market sentiment was further influenced by Anthropic's market debut on the Nasdaq, where the company achieved a valuation of approximately $2 trillion. Despite this milestone, US equities experienced sharp overnight declines as the broader AI sector tested investor appetite.

Meanwhile, international oil prices retreated, heading toward a weekly decline due to strong export figures from the Middle East. This downward trend persisted despite recent Houthi attacks targeting Riyadh in Saudi Arabia and reported disruptions involving tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Both Brent crude and West Texas Intermediate futures recorded notable drops over the week.

stories.title: Malaysian Palm Oil Futures Drop to Eight-Month Low on Weak Soyoil Prices
stories.summary:
Malaysian palm oil futures experienced a decline of over 2% on Friday, reaching their lowest closing price since March 5. The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange fell by 116 ringgit, equivalent to a 2.68% drop, to settle at 4,217 ringgit, or $1,026.28, per metric ton.

For the week, the contract lost 5.49%, marking its third weekly decline in a four-week period. According to David Ng, a proprietary trader at Iceberg X Sdn Bhd, the market has been under continuous pressure due to weaker soybean oil prices and remains closely tied to movements in both soybean oil and crude oil markets.

Regional competitor products also saw downward movement, with Dalian's most-active soyoil contract decreasing by 0.78% and its palm oil contract dropping by 1.4%. On the Chicago Board of Trade, soyoil prices recorded a decline of 0.88% as edible oils compete for global market share.

Additional pressure came from falling crude oil prices, which reduced the appeal of palm oil as a feedstock for biodiesel production. Despite ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, including Houthi attacks in Riyadh and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, strong regional exports pushed crude oil benchmarks down toward a weekly loss. The ringgit remained stable against the US dollar during the session.

stories.title: British Cybersecurity Experts Fix Vulnerability in Commercial Refrigeration Systems
stories.summary:
A British cybersecurity operation has successfully patched a flaw within the operating systems of commercial refrigerators and freezers used across supermarkets, restaurants, and warehouses. The intervention aims to protect local infrastructure from a wave of cyberattacks that recently impacted several European countries.

Earlier in November, similar cyber incidents disabled commercial cooling and freezing systems across nations from Sweden to Belgium, following an earlier hack in France in October. Those breaches forced businesses to discard millions of euros worth of perishable food. French intelligence agencies previously attributed the October attack, which struck 700 sites and caused 15 fires by manipulating internal refrigeration temperatures, to Iran's Revolutionary Guards.

Although the UK initially appeared unaffected because its refrigeration industry utilizes different equipment, ethical hackers at Omega Systems discovered a vulnerability that could have allowed similar breaches. Before the fix could be deployed, supermarkets disconnected their refrigeration units from the open internet as a precautionary measure to secure the devices.

German information security authorities had previously warned of ongoing vulnerabilities in industrial cooling equipment produced by Danish manufacturer Danfoss following the European attacks. While Britain's National Cyber Security Centre routinely issues proactive warning alerts regarding potential vulnerabilities, it declined to provide a comment on the recent findings.

stories.title: Lionel Messi Leads MLS Salaries With $28.3 Million Compensation Package
stories.summary:
Lionel Messi continues to hold the position of the highest-earning athlete in Major League Soccer, pulling in $28.3 million in guaranteed compensation. Figures published Thursday by the MLS Players Association show that the Argentine star's income increased by nearly $8 million compared to the previous year, though these totals strictly reflect playing compensation and exclude external revenue streams. Messi previously secured a contract extension running through the year 2028.

Robert Lewandowski of Poland secured the second spot overall after transferring to the Chicago Fire earlier in the year, earning $19.51 million. Following Lewandowski on the compensation list are Antoine Griezmann representing Orlando at $13.938 million, Son Heung-min playing for Los Angeles FC at $11.152 million, and Breel Embolo of Atlanta United at $10.81 million. The data reflect figures calculated up through October 9, including annualized amounts for athletes who transferred during the summer window.

At the club level, Inter Miami recorded the largest total guaranteed compensation at $59.37 million. Chicago followed in second place with $41.29 million, Atlanta placed third at $38.35 million, Los Angeles Galaxy took fourth at $34.91 million, and LAFC rounded out the top five with $32.91 million.

Conversely, the Philadelphia Union registered the lowest total team compensation in the league at $12.64 million. Sporting Kansas City recorded the second lowest at $13.30 million, while DC United registered the third lowest at $14.55 million.

stories.title: Opposition Alliance Faces Uncertainty After JUI-F Rejects Upcoming Conference
stories.summary:
The joint opposition faces a major setback regarding its planned All Parties Conference after the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl decided against participating. The political gathering is scheduled to take place in Lahore on November 24, but party representatives announced they would not attend because the event's agenda conflicts with their party manifesto and core demands. Additionally, JUI-F representatives pointed out that the position of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf concerning the upcoming conference remains ambiguous.

The withdrawal follows an initial formal gathering of the Tehreek Tahaffuz-e-Aain Pakistan organizing committee held in Islamabad on Wednesday to coordinate plans for the November event. Senator Kamran Murtaza represented the JUI-F at that preliminary session alongside PTI Chief Whip Aamir Dogar, Maulana Salahuddin Ayubi, and TTAP figures Hussain Ahmad Yousafzai and Khalid Yousaf Chaudhry.

During Wednesday's meeting, attendees examined initial preparations, settled preliminary arrangements, and deliberated on various administrative and consultative details. TTAP spokesperson Hussain Ahmad Yousafzai asserted at the time that all necessary measures would be implemented to conduct the conference successfully and on schedule.

The refusal by the JUI-F leaves the organizing committee's unified front in limbo as the scheduled date for the Lahore conference approaches. Organizers had intended for the coalition to present a cohesive front against the government through the scheduled consultations.

stories.title: Saudi-Led Coalition Urges Civilians to Evacuate Yemeni Port of Hodeidah
stories.summary:
The military coalition led by Saudi Arabia issued a public directive on Friday instructing residents to clear designated zones within the strategically vital Red Sea port city of Hodeidah. Authorities stated the measure was necessary to protect local civilians amidst escalating military engagements in the region.

The evacuation command follows a dramatic escalation of hostilities between the coalition and Houthi forces. Tensions heightened significantly after a recent missile and drone strike executed by the Houthi movement targeted Riyadh's tallest skyscraper on Thursday.

The ongoing conflict has seen continuous clashes across various fronts in Yemen. Alongside the developments in Hodeidah, Houthi forces have recently advanced their positions along Yemen's southern coast, moving progressively closer to Aden as the military campaign persists.

stories.title: Central Bank of Iran Adjusts Official Foreign Exchange Rates for Currencies
stories.summary:
The Central Bank of Iran released its official daily foreign exchange figures for November 19, revealing adjustments where the national currency registered changes against several major international currencies. Official metrics published by the central institution showed the exchange rate for the US dollar shifting to 1,936,329 rials, marking a change from the 1,932,464 rials recorded on November 18.

Additional adjustments included the Saudi riyal rising to 516,354 rials compared to 515,324 rials the previous day, while the UAE dirham climbed to 527,251 rials from 526,199 rials. For the Pakistani rupee, the official valuation was established at 700,140 rials for every 100 rupees, shifting from the prior day's rate of 698,900 rials, which calculates to roughly 7,001.4 rials per individual rupee. According to central bank data, across 34 tracked currencies on its trading platform, the national currency strengthened against the rial, whereas 12 other tracked currencies weakened.

These official valuations, distributed through the SANA platform utilized by licensed exchange establishments, remain substantially lower than rates found in parallel markets. Market sources indicate that on the parallel market, the dollar traded between 2.66 million and 2.69 million rials, while the euro ranged from 2.91 million to 2.94 million rials.

While official rates serve as the foundational benchmark for authorized foreign currency transactions, parallel market rates display much wider fluctuations. Regional markets monitoring trade flows and remittances involving the Pakistani rupee, Saudi riyal, and UAE dirham routinely evaluate both official and unofficial pricing indicators to assess current economic conditions.

stories.title: Significant Decline Recorded in Gold and Silver Prices Across Pakistan
stories.summary:
Gold and silver prices experienced a substantial drop in Pakistan, according to figures released by the All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association. The cost of gold per tola decreased by Rs15,400, bringing the rate down to Rs379,836. Additionally, 10 grams of 24-karat gold fell by Rs13,203 to reach Rs325,648, while 10 grams of 22-karat gold dropped by Rs12,103 to settle at Rs298,521. Internationally, gold prices decreased by $154, hitting $3,573 per ounce.

Precious metals also saw notable reductions in the domestic silver market. Silver fell by Rs297 to Rs4,708 per tola, and 10 grams of silver declined by Rs254 to Rs4,036. Global silver markets mirrored this downward trend, with prices falling by $2.97 to $42.30 per ounce. The All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association noted that domestic gold prices are established using interbank exchange rates.

Market experts explain that gold has encountered intense downward pressure due to widespread volatility, uncertainty surrounding the Iran conflict, high energy costs, shifts in artificial intelligence-related technology stocks, and mounting government debt. Despite its reputation as a safe-haven asset, these pressures have prompted analysts to reduce their 2026 gold price projections for a second consecutive quarter, driven by strong US Treasury yields and a robust dollar, based on a Reuters survey.

Looking ahead, analysts surveyed by Reuters anticipate that gold prices will likely bounce back by 2027. The same survey also indicated that predictions for platinum and palladium prices in 2026 were reduced for the third straight quarter. Meanwhile, in separate financial developments, Pakistan successfully acquired funding from the OPEC Fund and the Islamic Development Bank for three segments of the M-6 Motorway.

stories.title: Two Pakistani Educational Institutions Achieve International Recognition at Global Awards
stories.summary:
Two educational institutions in Pakistan have gained international distinction after being selected among the top contenders in their respective fields at the World’s Best School Prizes 2026. Managed by T4 Education, these awards are among the most esteemed global accolades in the education sector. Thousands of public and private institutions worldwide applied this year, and an international panel of experts reviewed the submissions across categories such as Community Collaboration, Environmental Action, Innovation, Overcoming Adversity, and Supporting Healthy Lives.

Representing Pakistan on the global stage were TNS Beaconhouse in Lahore and Govt Girls High School Tando Mir Ghulam Hussain in Hyderabad. TNS Beaconhouse emerged as the winner in the "Supporting Healthy Lives" category. Enrolling over 1,100 students across kindergarten, primary, and secondary grades, the Lahore-based private school was honored for its wellbeing-focused approach to integrating neurodivergent students, prioritizing confidence, inclusion, and student agency.

Meanwhile, the government-run high school in Hyderabad secured a spot among the world's top three finalists in the "Community Collaboration" category. Located in an impoverished region where girls often face early marriage or must contribute to household earnings, the Hyderabad school implemented a flexible learning model to support vulnerable working girls. By introducing a dual-shift system with morning and afternoon classes, the school accommodates students who work during daytime hours.

To build trust within the community, teachers conduct home visits to counsel parents on the long-term benefits of education, successfully challenging deeply entrenched cultural norms. Within a single year, these initiatives led to a 90 percent increase in enrollment and an 80 percent improvement in attendance. Furthermore, 80 percent of parents now prioritize schooling over child labor, reflecting a profound shift in community attitudes toward gender and education.

stories.title: How British Planters Transformed Tea into a South Asian Obsession
stories.summary:
Tea has become a deeply embedded part of daily life across India and Pakistan, consumed universally from office mornings to railway stations. However, this cultural staple was virtually unknown to the vast majority of South Asians a century ago, having originated as a British colonial cash crop rather than an indigenous domestic tradition.

Historically, Britain imported large quantities of Chinese tea, draining silver reserves until trade tensions prompted the East India Company to seek alternative sources. Following the discovery of wild Camellia sinensis bushes in Assam by Robert Bruce and local intermediaries, the first British tea garden was established in Chabua in 1837. Plantations expanded rapidly across Assam, Darjeeling, and the Nilgiris, eventually making India a major producer, though the output was almost entirely exported for an elite European and Anglophile minority.

As prices slumped in the early 20th century, planters faced a massive surplus and turned their attention to the untapped local market of 350 million people. Through organizations like the Tea Cess Committee and the Indian Tea Market Expansion Board, aggressive marketing campaigns distributed free samples, posters, and railway station vendors adapted the beverage by brewing stronger broken grades with milk, sugar, and local spices to create modern chai.

Today, the industry remains a massive economic force in the region. India continues to be one of the largest global producers and consumers, with domestic demand valued between $11.5 and $12 billion in 2024-25. Meanwhile, Pakistan stands as the world's largest tea importer by value, bringing in approximately 246,500 metric tonnes worth about $629 million during the 2024-25 fiscal year, primarily sourced from Kenya.

stories.title: Turkish Research Vessel Arrival Opens New Chapter in Energy Cooperation
stories.summary:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar welcomed the arrival of the Turkish seismic research vessel Oruc Reis in Karachi on Friday. Describing the event as a milestone in scientific research and strategic cooperation, Dar emphasized that Pakistan and Turkiye are eager to build a long-term energy partnership that includes offshore exploration, minerals, and renewable energy.

The welcome ceremony was attended by several high-ranking officials, including Sindh Governor Nihal Hashmi, Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik, and Turkish Minister for Energy and Natural Resources Alparslan Bayraktar. Dar praised the longstanding fraternal ties between the two nations and thanked Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan for their commitment to strengthening bilateral relations.

Turkish Minister Alparslan Bayraktar stated that the Oruc Reis completed a 19-day voyage to reach Pakistan and will spend approximately two months conducting a three-dimensional seismic survey in offshore waters of Sindh and Makran. The Turkish Petroleum Corporation will handle data acquisition in collaboration with Pakistani energy firms such as OGDCL, PPL, and Mari Energies, following the completion of licensing processes for five blocks.

Both nations stressed the importance of sustainable development, environmental protection, and maritime security as part of these joint ventures. The collaboration aligns with discussions held between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Erdogan in Antalya regarding the swift implementation of cooperative initiatives in trade, investment, defence, and energy.

stories.title: Kozo Tashima Dismisses Plans to Withdraw from Upcoming FIFA Presidency Race
stories.summary:
FIFA presidential candidate Kozo Tashima stated on Friday that he has no immediate intention of dropping out of the election to create a two-way contest between current president Gianni Infantino and French football chief Philippe Diallo. Tashima, a former Japan Football Association president and current FIFA Council member, is one of three official candidates for the March election.

While Diallo enjoys strong European backing and is viewed as a primary challenger to unseat Infantino, Tashima emphasized his desire to work closely with the French official given his governance experience. Diallo had previously expressed interest in holding talks to join forces against Infantino, a move Tashima welcomed without viewing Diallo as a direct opponent in their shared goal of reforming the organization.

Tashima's campaign centers on restoring integrity, transparency, and trust within world football's governing body. Although he acknowledged that Infantino has achieved positive outcomes since taking office in 2016, Tashima noted that recent events surrounding the World Cup convinced him that change is necessary. Specifically, he criticized FIFA's decision to lift a ban on US player Folarin Balogun following an intervention by US President Donald Trump.

Turning 69 on Saturday, Tashima defended his low-key approach to leadership, asserting that the primary spotlight should remain on players, referees, and teams rather than the FIFA president. Having led the JFA from 2016 to 2024, Tashima maintains that running for the presidency is the most effective path to improving the global institution.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Strengthens Past 93 Mark Amid Record Foreign Stock Inflows
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee strengthened past the psychologically crucial 93-per-dollar threshold on Friday, achieving its strongest level since April. This movement marks a significant turnaround for the currency, which had faced severe downward pressure earlier in the year and approached record lows near 97 last month. Year-to-date losses have now been reduced to approximately 3%, down from a peak of nearly 8% in May. 

The currency's appreciation was driven by a surge in foreign investments into Indian equities, as global investors sought refuge from a wider rout in artificial intelligence-linked markets. Foreign investors poured a record $12 billion into Indian shares in November, reversing a prolonged selling trend that saw over $60 billion exit the market between September 2024 and October 2026. This massive inflow greatly increased the supply of US dollars within the financial system. 

Additional support for the rupee came from declining oil prices and deliberate policy measures implemented by the Reserve Bank of India. The central bank has worked to curb domestic demand for dollars by cracking down on speculative trades, attracting funds from overseas citizens, and shifting oil-import-related currency demand away from the spot market. Furthermore, RBI chief Sanjay Malhotra had previously indicated that monetary tightening remained an option to protect the currency.

Market participants also noted a rapid unwinding of bearish wagers against the rupee, particularly by overseas hedge funds operating in offshore and non-deliverable forward markets. Analysts highlighted that the Reserve Bank of India has deliberately allowed the local currency to appreciate rather than intervening to build foreign reserves, intending to shift expectations among exporters and offshore traders.

stories.title: Thar Coal Project Benefits Entire Country, States Sindh Minister Memon
stories.summary:
Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon stated on Friday that electricity generated from the Thar coal project is supplying the national grid and benefiting consumers across Pakistan. Speaking at a green energy event, Memon credited the initiative to a vision originally outlined by the late Benazir Bhutto and later advanced by Asif Ali Zardari in 2008, after previous delays under the PML-N government. He described past failures to extract Thar coal in a timely manner as criminal negligence, noting that the provincial government has invested $1 billion into extraction efforts.

Memon also highlighted various renewable energy and social welfare programs undertaken in Sindh. He mentioned that the provincial administration established solar parks and the Jhimpir wind energy project, while distributing free solar panels, fans, and lights to millions of households. Additionally, Sindh pioneered the introduction of electric buses and launched programs to provide free scooters and rural training to empower women.

Despite these energy contributions, Memon sharply criticized the ongoing electricity situation in rural areas of Sindh. He pointed out that residents face severe power outages lasting between 16 and 20 hours daily. He attributed this prolonged load-shedding to the inefficiency of regional utility providers including K-Electric, the Hyderabad Electric Supply Company, and the Sukkur Electric Power Company, adding that high electricity costs have made bills increasingly unaffordable for citizens.

stories.title: Indian Equities Defy Global Tech Slump to Secure Fourth Weekly Gain
stories.summary:
Indian stock markets defied a severe global rout in technology shares on Friday, securing a fourth consecutive weekly gain. The benchmark Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex rose by 2.6% and 2.9% respectively over the week, both closing at nine-month highs of 25,800.6 and 83,919.71. Both indexes advanced 1.1% on Friday alone, contrasting sharply with broader Asian equities, which headed toward their worst weekly performance since 2020 amid ongoing declines in artificial intelligence supply-chain stocks.

The resilience of Indian equities stems from a significant rotation of global capital into the country as investors pursue value-buying alternatives away from troubled AI markets. Foreign institutional investors injected a record $12.21 billion into Indian shares during the month of November. This influx of capital also propelled the Indian rupee past the 93-per-dollar mark for the first time since April, supported by easing oil prices and positive economic projections from financial institutions like HSBC and Goldman Sachs.

Sector performance varied across the market during the week, with twelve of the sixteen major sectors posting gains. Financials and banking stocks led the advance, climbing 3.7% and 5.9% respectively to reach record highs. Conversely, metal stocks dropped 3% due to softer commodity prices and concerns over slower data-center investments, while small-caps dipped 1.1% and mid-caps remained mostly flat. Automobile stocks rose 3.1% on the back of robust festival-season sales and lower input costs.

stories.title: مصنوعی ذہانت کی کمپنی اینتھروپک کے بانی مارکیٹ میں حصص فروخت کرکے ارب پتی بن گئے
stories.summary:
مصنوعی ذہانت کی کمپنی اینتھروپک نے پہلی بار شیئر مارکیٹ میں اپنے حصص فروخت کیے ہیں، جن سے کمپنی کو 81 ارب ڈالر حاصل ہوئے ہیں۔ اس پیش رفت کے بعد یہ دنیا کی سب سے بڑی کمپنیوں میں شامل ہو گئی ہے۔ کمپنی نے اپنے ایک شیئر کی قیمت 83 ڈالر مقرر کی اور یہ حصص نیویارک سٹاک مارکیٹ میں ٹریڈنگ کے لیے پیش کیے گئے۔ صرف پانچ برسوں میں اینتھروپک ایک کم معروف سٹارٹ اپ سے بڑھ کر ایسی ٹیکنالوجی کمپنی بن چکی ہے جس کی مالیت ایک ٹریلین ڈالر سے زیادہ ہے۔

2021 میں قائم ہونے والی اینتھروپک کے ساتوں بانی سٹاک مارکیٹ میں ٹریڈ کے بعد فوری طور پر ارب پتی بن جائیں گے۔ اس کی متوقع مالیت 1.75 ٹریلین ڈالر تک ہو جائے گی۔ کمپنی کی آمدنی میں بھی تیزی سے اضافہ ہوا ہے اور رواں سال ستمبر تک کے نو ماہ میں آمدنی 33 ارب ڈالر رہی، تاہم اسی عرصے میں اس کا نقصان 104 ارب ڈالر تک پہنچ گیا۔ کمپنی کے اے آئی ٹولز کوڈنگ، تحریر اور معلومات کا خلاصہ تیار کرنے جیسے کاموں میں استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔

اینتھروپک مجموعی طور پر 107 ارب ڈالر حاصل کر سکتی ہے جس میں 81 ارب ڈالر حصص فروخت کر کے اور 26 ارب ڈالر گوگل، مائیکروسافٹ اور اینویڈیا سمیت کئی ٹیکنالوجی کمپنیوں کی سرمایہ کاری سے آئیں گے۔ اس سے پہلے جون میں ایلون مسک کی کمپنی سپیس ایکس نے آئی پی او کے ذریعے 75 ارب ڈالر حاصل کیے تھے۔ اینتھروپک کی بنیاد اوپن اے آئی کے سات سابق ملازمین نے رکھی تھی اور اس کی قیادت بہن بھائی ڈاریو امودی اور ڈینیلا امودیئی کر رہے ہیں۔

ڈاریو امودی 43 سالہ چیف ایگزیکٹو ہیں جبکہ ڈینیلا امودیئی 39 سالہ صدر کے طور پر روزمرہ انتظامی امور کی نگرانی کرتی ہیں۔ دیگر بانیوں میں چیف کمپیوٹ آفیسر ٹام براؤن، عوامی مفاد کے امور کی سربراہ جیک کلارک اور چیف سائنس آفیسر جیرڈ کپلان شامل ہیں۔ یہ تمام بانی مصنوعی ذہانت کے ممکنہ خطرات کے پیش نظر حفاظت اور ضابطہ کاری پر بھی زور دیتے ہیں جبکہ کاروبار کو تیزی سے وسعت دے رہے ہیں۔

stories.title: British-Pakistani Entrepreneur Nasir Younas Awarded Freedom of the City of London
stories.summary:
Nasir Younas, a British-Pakistani businessman who moved to London from Lahore as a teenager carrying 200 pounds and speaking limited English, was awarded the Freedom of the City of London during a ceremony at the Chamberlain's Court at Guildhall. He received the historic honor in recognition of his contributions to business, the hospitality sector, and philanthropy across the United Kingdom.

Surrounded by family, friends, and figures from public and business life, Younas completed the traditional process by reading the Declaration of a Freeman and signing the Register of Freemen. Dating back to 1237, the Freedom honor has previously been awarded to notable historical figures, including members of the royal family, prime ministers, world leaders, and prominent artists and scientists.

Reflecting on his journey, Younas shared that he arrived in the British capital in 2004 with money borrowed by his father and no network to guide him. He described receiving the recognition as the proudest moment of his working life, crediting London for educating and shaping him after he initially intended to earn money and return home.

Grows up in Ghoray Shah near Lahore as the eldest son of a shopkeeper, Younas began helping at his father's grocery store at age fourteen. Upon reaching London, his earliest employment involved boiling rice in an Oxford Street restaurant basement from morning until evening for forty pounds a day.

stories.title: Pakistan Holds Eight to Ten Trillion Dollars in Natural Resources, Says Dar
stories.summary:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar stated that Pakistan possesses minerals, hydrocarbons, and other natural resources valued between $8 trillion and $10 trillion, calling this a highly conservative estimate. Dar made these remarks during a Karachi ceremony welcoming the Oruç Reis, a Turkish seismic research vessel that arrived to conduct offshore oil and gas exploration. He praised the collaboration between Turkish petroleum experts and Pakistani national energy companies, emphasizing that geological data is essential for future exploration.

Describing offshore exploration as a complex, capital-intensive, and uncertain endeavor, Dar noted that seismic surveys do not guarantee commercial discoveries, though they are a necessary first step. He expressed Pakistan's desire for a long-term energy partnership with Turkiye spanning offshore exploration, minerals, and renewable energy, noting that several memorandums of understanding have been signed. He also stressed that all maritime activities must adhere to strict environmental protection and safety standards.

According to Turkish officials, the vessel's seismic mission will last approximately five to six months. Responding to critics who characterize Pakistan as being trapped in debt, Dar asserted that the total estimated value of the nation's natural resources—including mines, minerals, hydrocarbons, gemstones, and rare earth materials—far exceeds its financial liabilities.

The arrival of the Oruç Reis marks the resumption of offshore exploration after nearly a two-decade hiatus, following the launch of the Offshore Bid Round 2025. The Turkish Petroleum Corporation's subsidiary, TPOC, has partnered with local entities like OGDCL, Mari Energies, and PPL to explore multiple blocks. Although Pakistan's offshore zone covers roughly 300,000 square kilometers, only 18 wells have been drilled there since 1947, leaving substantial untapped potential identified by US firm DeGolyer and MacNaughton.

stories.title: Narowal Mother Arrested for Suffocating Three Young Children to Death
stories.summary:
Police in Narowal have arrested a mother and two other suspects following the alleged murders of her three young children over the course of a month. District Police Officer Narowal stated that the crimes were uncovered after the woman's husband became suspicious of her behavior. Investigators revealed that the suspect also attempted to take the life of a fourth child, who survived the ordeal unharmed.

According to the initial police findings, the mother confessed to killing her five-year-old son Mosa, three-year-old daughter Khadija, and one-year-old son Naqeeb by suffocating them with a cloth. The tragic events took place in the Dadipur area, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Saddar Police Station in Shakargarh, Narowal.

Authorities have registered a formal case at the Saddar Shakargarh Police Station against the arrested individuals. Police indicated that the suspect was allegedly involved in an extramarital affair, which is currently being examined as part of the ongoing investigation into the motive behind the killings.

stories.title: اسلام آباد میں 13 سالہ گھریلو ملازمہ کی ہلاکت، ملزمان کے جسمانی ریمانڈ میں توسیع
stories.summary:
اسلام آباد میں 13 سالہ گھریلو ملازمہ فاطمہ کی مبینہ تشدد سے ہلاکت کے مقدمے میں عدالت نے گرفتار دونوں ملزمان کے جسمانی ریمانڈ میں مزید تین روز کی توسیع کر دی ہے۔ ڈسٹرکٹ اینڈ سیشن کورٹ اسلام آباد میں جوڈیشل مجسٹریٹ نائمہ عفت کے روبرو سماعت ہوئی جہاں پراسیکیوشن نے بتایا کہ ملزمہ سے ایک الیکٹرک آئرن اور شریک ملزم قاری علی سے ایک ڈنڈا برآمد کیا گیا ہے۔ سی سی ٹی وی ریکارڈ میں بچی پر بار بار تشدد کی ویڈیوز بھی موجود ہیں جنہیں فرانزک کے لیے بھجوا دیا گیا ہے۔

یہ واقعہ 15 نومبر کو پیش آیا تھا جس کے بعد قتل کی دفعات کے تحت مقدمہ درج کیا گیا۔ پراسیکیوشن کے مطابق بچی گزشتہ تین برس سے گھر میں مقیم تھی اور پوسٹ مارٹم رپورٹ میں اس کے جسم پر تشدد اور جلائے جانے کے 20 نشانات پائے گئے ہیں۔ کم سن بچی ایک سرکاری افسر کی رہائش گاہ پر ان کی اہلیہ کے پاس ملازمت کرتی تھی جو کہ غیر ملکی شہریت بھی رکھتی ہیں اور یہ رہائش گاہ اسلام آباد پولیس لائنز ہیڈ کوارٹرز میں واقع ہے۔

متاثرہ بچی کو تشویشناک حالت میں اسلام آباد کے قائداعظم ہسپتال منتقل کیا گیا تھا لیکن وہ جانبر نہ ہو سکی۔ تفتیشی ٹیم کے مطابق مقتولہ کے والدین مذکورہ پولیس افسر کی رحیم یار خان میں واقع زمینوں پر کام کرتے ہیں۔ ملزمہ کے شوہر اس وقت وفاقی تحقیقاتی ادارے (ایف آئی اے) میں گوجرانوالہ ریجن میں بطور ڈائریکٹر خدمات انجام دے رہے ہیں۔ اس مقدمے میں گرفتار دوسرا ملزم قاری علی پنجاب ہائی ویز پٹرولنگ میں تعینات سرکاری ملازم ہے۔

پوسٹ مارٹم رپورٹ کے مطابق فاطمہ کی موت بار بار کیے جانے والے جسمانی تشدد کے نتیجے میں لگنے والی شدید چوٹوں سے ہوئی۔ ڈاکٹروں نے سر کے پچھلے حصے میں سوجن، چہرے، بازوؤں اور ٹانگوں پر نیل اور استری سے جلائے جانے کے نشانات کی تصدیق کی ہے۔ اسلام آباد پولیس کے حکام کا کہنا ہے کہ واقعے کے ہر پہلو سے شفاف تحقیقات کی جا رہی ہیں اور پوسٹ مارٹم رپورٹ کی روشنی میں مزید قانونی کارروائی عمل میں لائی جائے گی۔

stories.title: Gold prices decline sharply across Pakistan following international market trends
stories.summary:
Gold prices in Pakistan experienced a significant drop on Friday, mirroring losses observed in the global market. According to the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, the local price of gold per tola fell by Rs15,400, settling at Rs379,836. 

Additionally, the cost of 10-gram gold decreased by Rs13,203 to reach Rs325,648. This downturn follows a previous decline on Thursday, when the per-tola gold price had dropped by Rs3,700 to reach Rs395,236.

Globally, the international rate of gold fell by $154, bringing the price down to $3,573 per ounce. Alongside the precious metal, the price of silver in the domestic market also saw a reduction, dropping by Rs297 to reach Rs4,708 per tola.

stories.title: Karachi faces worsening wheat crisis and potential flour mill closures
stories.summary:
Karachi's wheat crisis has escalated significantly, creating widespread concerns over potential flour shortages and the prospective shutdown of local flour mills. This situation stems from an ongoing deadlock between the Sindh Food Department and flour millers regarding the retail cost of flour milled from government-imported wheat.

While imported wheat has begun arriving at mills for Rs5,000 per bag, agreement on flour pricing remains out of reach. Flour mill representatives have proposed supplying flour made from government wheat at Rs146 per kilogram, whereas the Sindh government insists on a capped price of Rs140 per kilogram. Negotiations between the Food Department and millers have failed to produce a consensus.

Flour mill representative Malik Iqbal noted that mills in Karachi are currently collecting imported wheat directly from Karachi Port, while mills in interior Sindh await government wheat shipments despite issued permits. Meanwhile, an open-market wheat shortage has enabled profiteers to charge arbitrary rates, worsening conditions.

The Flour Mills Association warned that the supply-demand gap has reached a critical stage and cautioned that mills may shut down completely if supplies are not secured. The association has urged the government to ensure continuous distribution and permit private sector imports to avert further deterioration before December.

stories.title: Ringleader pleads guilty to record $100 million California jewellery heist
stories.summary:
The ringleader of a notorious highway robbery gang pleaded guilty to a federal charge in connection with the theft of approximately $100 million in jewellery from an armoured vehicle in California five years ago. The incident stands as the largest jewellery heist in United States history.

The defendant, 33-year-old Ecuadorean national Carlos Victor Mestanza Cercado, entered his guilty plea to a single felony count of interference with commerce by robbery under an agreement with prosecutors. Arrested two years ago during a flight layover in Panama, Mestanza was among seven individuals indicted for the July 11, 2022, robbery of a Brink's truck at a Kern County rest stop north of Los Angeles. The vehicle was transporting 73 sacks of precious gems, fine gold, diamonds, rubies, emeralds, and luxury watches from a San Francisco Bay area exhibition to a Southern California storage facility.

Authorities stated that Mestanza and his accomplices trailed the shipment across 380 miles using multiple vehicles and cellphones to coordinate. They breached the locks of the parked armoured truck and escaped with 24 bags of valuables. In exchange for his guilty plea, prosecutors dropped several other charges against Mestanza, and his sentencing is scheduled for April 15, carrying a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison.

Beyond the major jewellery theft, Mestanza also admitted involvement in the March 2022 highway robberies of trucks transporting electronics. Among his co-defendants, three are scheduled for trial in March 2027, two remain at large, and one has been deported. It remains unclear whether any of the stolen jewellery has been recovered.

stories.title: Former federal minister Liaquat Abbas Bhatti murdered in Hafizabad home
stories.summary:
Former federal minister Liaquat Abbas Bhatti was found murdered inside his room near Kasoki Bypass in Hafizabad, with local police reporting that he was strangled to death. An initial medical examination indicated clear marks of strangulation caused by a rope around his neck.

A murder and robbery case has been filed at the City Police Station following a complaint by the victim's nephew, Member of the Provincial Assembly Zameer-ul-Hassan Bhatti. The First Information Report names more than 10 suspects, including four of the former minister's personal security guards, who allegedly carried out the strangulation before fleeing the scene.

According to police reports, the perpetrators also stole 50 tolas of gold jewellery, Rs2 million in cash, weapons, and three luxury vehicles belonging to the deceased. District Police Officer Fawad Ahmed stated that specialized police teams have been deployed to track down and arrest all individuals connected to the crime.

Liaquat Abbas Bhatti had a prominent political career, having previously served twice as a Member of the National Assembly and once as a Member of the Provincial Assembly.

stories.title: Field Marshal Munir Visits North Waziristan to Review Regional Security
stories.summary:
Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, travelled to Miran Shah in North Waziristan on Friday to evaluate the ongoing security conditions and counterterrorism operations in the region. Upon arriving, he placed a floral wreath at the Yadgar-e-Shuhada to honor soldiers who lost their lives while performing their official duties. During the visit, the army chief was given a comprehensive briefing regarding the local security framework, intelligence-based operations, and the strategies being implemented to preserve hard-earned counterterrorism gains and secure lasting stability.

During his time in the area, Field Marshal Munir interacted directly with military officers and troops, commending their professional readiness, high morale, and dedication to safeguarding the nation. He specifically lauded the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police, characterizing them as a courageous frontline unit and expressing admiration for their resilience and sacrifices in combating terrorism throughout the province. He reiterated that security forces, working alongside other law enforcement agencies, remain fully committed to eradicating terrorism and preserving peace.

The high-ranking military official was officially greeted upon his arrival by the Commander Peshawar Corps, according to an official statement released by the Inter-Services Public Relations. The visit underscores ongoing military oversight in border regions and highlights the collaborative efforts between the military and local police forces to maintain public safety and regional order against persistent militant threats.

stories.title: Pochettino Faces Tough Liverpool Test as Manchester United Struggles Continue
stories.summary:
Mauricio Pochettino begins his tenure as manager of Manchester United with a challenging fixture away against rivals Liverpool this weekend. The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss takes over a struggling squad that sits in the Premier League relegation zone and could potentially drop to the bottom of the table depending on prior results. Under departed manager Michael Carrick, the team accumulated only eight points from their first 10 matches, marking their lowest points tally at this stage of a league campaign in 40 years. Following the Anfield encounter, United face upcoming matches against Brentford, Newcastle, Coventry, and Crystal Palace.

In other Premier League action, second-placed Brighton aim to sustain momentum after winning six of their last seven league games. Under Fabian Hurzeler, the south-coast club boasts the league's top-scoring attack with 26 goals and has conceded only seven, though midfielder Pascal Gross dismissed talk of an early title challenge. Meanwhile, Manchester City are seeking to halt a three-match losing streak that leaves them six points behind leaders Arsenal. Enzo Maresca's side faces Fulham, a team City has defeated in their last 20 encounters across all competitions, as the club continues to await potential penalties regarding over 100 alleged breaches of financial regulations.

stories.title: India Capitalizes on New Zealand Errors After Nicholls Scores Unbeaten 175
stories.summary:
India capitalized on several fielding mistakes by New Zealand to reach 159-1 by the conclusion of the second day in the first Test at Wellington, trailing the hosts by 209 runs. Opening batters Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul forged a 130-run stand in just 27.5 overs, exploiting early dropped catches. Jaiswal, who contributed 85 runs from 89 balls, was dropped twice on zero and six by Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips, while Rahul survived an unreviewed lbw appeal on five. Jaiswal played aggressively, striking numerous boundaries before being caught behind off Matt Henry, leaving Rahul unbeaten on 52 alongside Devdutt Padikkal on 16 at stumps.

Earlier on day two, New Zealand were dismissed for 368 shortly after lunch, driven by Nicholls' patient, unbeaten 175 off 335 balls. Nicholls anchored the innings alongside Phillips, whose 118 helped rescue the team from an early collapse at 70-5 on the first day through a 216-run partnership. Indian fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah returned to Test cricket after a year to claim 4-92, supported by Akash Deep who took 3-53. Indian bowlers struggled with their lengths during parts of the innings, but the top-order batters responded with swift scoring to press for a result on a pitch becoming increasingly favorable for batting.

stories.title: Cyber Crime Agency Arrests Suspect in Karachi Over Stolen US Data Sale
stories.summary:
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency arrested a suspect in Karachi accused of acquiring, possessing, and selling confidential data belonging to United States government agencies, law enforcement organizations, and private companies. A formal criminal case has been registered at the agency's Karachi police station under multiple sections of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016, following amendments in 2025. Investigators stated that the suspect operated under the online alias 'DP BRUCE' and utilized platforms like LeakBase and Telegram to advertise stolen databases containing sensitive information linked to institutions such as the FBI, CIA, Department of State, Department of Defence, and various police departments.

According to the agency, the suspect allegedly received payments for the compromised information through cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin. Acting on credible intelligence, an NCCIA team conducted a raid in Karachi's Manzoor Colony on November 11, apprehending the suspect and seizing a personal laptop. Preliminary technical inspections of the device revealed multiple files and databases containing sensitive US records and evidence of online trade activities. The agency emphasized its ongoing commitment to dismantling cybercriminal networks involved in domestic and transnational illicit data trading.

The arrest forms part of a broader series of enforcement actions by the cyber crime agency. Just a day prior, the NCCIA reported uncovering a financial network tied to illegal online betting, fraudulent operations, and money laundering with transactions reaching up to Rs1 trillion. Earlier in the month, the agency also detained numerous suspects across various operations targeting international cyber fraud networks, illegal call centers, and unauthorized data sales.

stories.title: Punjab Revenue Authority Warns Hotels and Restaurants Over Digital Payments
stories.summary:
The Punjab Revenue Authority has announced that it will take strict measures against hotels and restaurants that obstruct the digital payment system across the province. The warning was shared by a spokesperson following a high-level meeting on promoting digital transactions.

Chaired by PRA Chairman Moazzam Iqbal Sappra, the meeting established that forgery in payment records and tax misappropriation will face zero tolerance. Authorities confirmed that establishments compelling customers to pay exclusively in cash will be placed under strict surveillance.

Businesses utilizing unregistered Point of Sale systems or depositing funds into unauthorized bank accounts will be subjected to heavy financial penalties. Furthermore, the PRA has instructed its vigilance wing to inspect and verify business receipts and payment records across multiple districts in Punjab.

stories.title: Tim Hortons App Shared User Data with Israeli Tech Firm, Says Group
stories.summary:
Canadians for Justice and Peace in the Middle East stated that the mobile application for coffee chain Tim Hortons shares sensitive consumer information with Forter, an Israeli fraud prevention company established by alumni of the Israeli military intelligence Unit 8200. The advocacy group urged the company to sever ties with the technology firm, having confirmed its identity with assistance from University of Calgary researcher Joel Reardon, whose findings appeared in a CBC investigation.

The investigation revealed that the Tim Hortons app transmitted details such as unique device identifiers, camera specs, and nearby Wi-Fi networks to third parties, with researcher Joel Reardon describing the data collection as excessive. CJPME Vice President Michael Bueckert criticized the sharing of personal data with a cyber-tech company linked to a foreign military intelligence unit tied to human rights violations against Palestinians. Microsoft previously restricted cloud and AI services used by Unit 8200 over surveillance concerns.

In response to the CBC report, Tim Hortons stated that the information is gathered strictly for fraud prevention, payment protection, and account security rather than marketing purposes. The company maintained that third parties are prohibited from selling the data and that it does not sell user information. Previously, in 2022, Canadian privacy regulators determined the coffee chain's app gathered extensive location data without proper user consent.

stories.title: US Dollar Nears 19-Month High Amid Federal Reserve Tightening Bets
stories.summary:
The United States dollar hovered near a 19-month high, remaining on track for a fourth consecutive week of gains driven by expectations of further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and investor safe-haven demand amid artificial intelligence market jitters. The dollar index traded near 103.9, its strongest level since early April 2025. The rally intensified after November 10 when strong US inflation data bolstered tightening expectations and Fed Governor Christopher Waller suggested a potential 50-basis-point increase in December. This currency strength coincided with weak equity sentiment, dragging the S&P 500 down for six straight sessions amid broader concerns over tech valuations.

Additional support for the greenback came from hawkish statements by regional Federal Reserve officials. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson noted that interest rates must rise due to high inflation, while Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee stated that inflation data does not indicate price pressures are returning naturally to the 2% target. Conversely, the Japanese yen firmed 0.3% to 159.13 against the dollar following data showing Japan's annual core inflation accelerated to 2.2% in October. Meanwhile, sterling languished near a one-year low of $1.3106, the euro struggled near $1.0977, the Australian dollar hovered close to $0.6664, and China's offshore yuan bounced to 6.743 per dollar.

In regional developments, the Punjab Revenue Authority in Lahore warned of strict enforcement against hotels and restaurants obstructing digital payment systems. PRA Chairman Moazzam Iqbal Sappra led a meeting focused on expanding digital transactions and curbing tax evasion and forgery across the province.

This currency market movement matters because it reflects global investor anxiety regarding technology sector valuations and shifting macroeconomic forecasts. Higher interest rate expectations in the United States directly influence global capital flows, impacting currency valuations and borrowing costs internationally.

stories.title: Trump, Xi, and Putin Hold Historic Trilateral Summit in Shenzhen
stories.summary:
The leaders of the world's three major powers convened for an unprecedented 90-minute trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin gathered at a hillside resort to address international stability. Although the talks concluded with a joint peace declaration and four key agreements—including plans to reform the United Nations, increase refined petroleum supplies, and launch nuclear risk reduction dialogues—analysts widely characterized the session as a confidence-building exercise rather than an immediate resolution to ongoing global conflicts.

During the discussions, which also touched upon the war in Ukraine and the jurisdictions of bodies like the International Criminal Court, each leader emphasized the necessity of major-power cooperation. Xi highlighted that regular high-level engagement is essential for crisis prevention. Trump advocated for reduced nuclear stockpiles while criticizing globalist organizations, and Putin emphasized shared responsibilities regarding international security and transnational crime. According to regional experts like Hoo Tiang Boon and Wu Xinbo, Beijing and Moscow emerged as the primary beneficiaries, with China successfully showcasing its diplomatic centrality as host and Russia utilizing the platform to counter global isolation. Trump's participation was viewed as an effort to project international leadership following domestic midterm setbacks.

Despite the positive optics and descriptions of the talks as constructive by all three leaders, skepticism persists regarding tangible outcomes. Scholars noted that the joint statement lacked substantive progress on complex geopolitical issues such as the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. However, analysts suggest that establishing direct communication channels creates positive momentum and reinforces mutual trust, pointing to the potential for future institutionalized trilateral interactions in an uncertain global landscape.

stories.title: اٹلی کے خطے پوگلیا کی روایتی روٹی فریزیلے جو سال بھر خراب نہیں ہوتی
stories.summary:
جنوبی اٹلی کے خطے پوگلیا کی روایتی روٹی فریزیلے اپنی انفرادیت اور طویل مدتِ تحفظ کی وجہ سے دنیا بھر میں جانی جاتی ہے۔ اس گول اور پتھر جیسی سخت روٹی کو کھانے سے پہلے پانی میں ڈبویا جاتا ہے تاکہ اس کی خستگی برقرار رہتے ہوئے یہ نرم ہو جائے۔ مقامی لوگ اس پر ٹماٹر، زیتون کے تیل میں محفوظ مرچیں، کیپرز، اوریگانو اور لہسن کے ساتھ بینگن ڈال کر استعمال کرتے ہیں۔ یہ طریقہ صدیوں پرانا ہے اور اس خطے کی تاریخ سے جڑا ہوا ہے۔

فریزیلے کی تیاری کا عمل نہایت دلچسپ اور دو مراحل پر مشتمل ہوتا ہے۔ بیکر آٹے کی لمبی پٹی بنا کر اسے حلقے کی شکل میں ڈھالتے ہیں اور تقریباً چالیس منٹ تک بیک کرتے ہیں۔ اس کے بعد اسے تار کی مدد سے کاٹا جاتا ہے تاکہ اس کی سطح کھردری ہو جائے اور یہ ذائقہ اور پانی بہتر طریقے سے جذب کر سکے۔ کٹنے کے بعد اسے دوبارہ تقریباً ڈیڑھ گھنٹے کے لیے تنور میں رکھا جاتا ہے تاکہ اس میں موجود تمام نمی ختم ہو جائے اور پھپھوندی نہ لگ سکے۔

اس روٹی کی تاریخ ہزاروں سال پرانی ہے اور قدیم دور میں ملاح اور کسان طویل سفر کے دوران اسے اپنے ساتھ رکھتے تھے۔ پوگلیا کے ساحلی اور زرعی ماحول کے پیشِ نظر یہ خوراک سمندری سفر اور جنگ و امن کے ادوار میں انتہائی کارآمد ثابت ہوئی۔ فولا جیوردانو کے مطابق پہلی صدی عیسوی میں بھی دو بار بیک کی جانے والی ملاحوں کی روٹی کا ذکر ملتا ہے جسے صلیبی اور زائرین بھی استعمال کرتے تھے۔

وقت کے ساتھ اس روٹی کی تیاری میں استعمال ہونے والے اناج میں بھی تبدیلی آئی ہے۔ ماضی میں جو سے بنے فریزیلے کو غریبوں کی خوراک سمجھا جاتا تھا اور لوگ گندم کو ترجیح دیتے تھے، لیکن اب جو کے فریزیلے زیادہ صحت بخش اور مقبول متبادل بن چکے ہیں۔ آج کل پوگلیا کی بیکریوں میں اس کی مختلف اقسام دستیاب ہیں جن میں سپیلٹ اور ملٹی گرین شامل ہیں، جبکہ شیف اب اسے جدید انداز میں ڈیکنسٹرکٹڈ ڈشز اور چھوٹے سائز میں بھی پیش کر رہے ہیں۔

stories.title: US Religious Freedom Panel Accuses India of Targeting Muslim Minorities
stories.summary:
The United States Commission on International Religious Freedom stated that India has escalated its targeting of religious minorities during a massive nationwide voter list revision. USCIRF Chair Asif Mahmood reported that Muslim citizens are being systematically removed from voter rolls, labeled as foreigners, and illegally deported. The electoral revision resulted in the deletion of 130 million names—the largest such reduction in Indian history—with data showing disproportionate impacts on Muslims, India's largest minority group. This community has faced increasing discrimination since Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party assumed power in 2014.

India's Election Commission defended the voter roll updates, stating the process targeted duplicate, deceased, and ineligible voters while offering an appeals mechanism for anyone excluded in error. However, commissioner Gene Mills urged the US State Department to designate India as a country of particular concern, citing the expulsion of citizens based on faith. The Indian foreign ministry dismissed USCIRF as biased and viewed its criticism as foreign interference in domestic affairs. Meanwhile, opposition groups and student demonstrators have staged protests against the revisions, leading to crackdowns that have drawn further criticism from international human rights experts.

This controversy underscores deepening international scrutiny over minority rights in India. While government officials maintain that state policies benefit all communities through welfare and infrastructure programs, international bodies and civil rights advocates point to rising hate speech, discriminatory citizenship legislation, and administrative actions as evidence of systemic prejudice against religious minorities.

stories.title: Pakistan Climbs 17 Spots in United Nations E-Government Index 2026
stories.summary:
Pakistan advanced 17 positions globally in the United Nations E-Government Development Index 2026, reaching the 119th spot according to an official statement. This latest achievement brings the nation's total ranking improvement to 31 places over the past four years, demonstrating measurable progress in digital governance and the digital delivery of public services. Pakistan's EGDI score rose by 23 percent to reach 0.6264, accompanied by significant regional advancements in online public service delivery across South Asia.

Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima attributed the upgraded ranking to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's objective of establishing a digital nation. She noted that coordinated initiatives between federal and provincial authorities have successfully transitioned numerous government services to online platforms, thereby improving accessibility for everyday citizens. The minister emphasized that this upward trajectory in digital infrastructure has garnered international acknowledgment for the country's reform efforts.

The UN E-Government Survey, compiled biennially by the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs, evaluates all 193 UN member states using three core dimensions: online services, telecommunications infrastructure, and human capital. Participating nations are categorized into four distinct groups and 16 rating classes, with the highest tier designating the most sophisticated e-government systems worldwide. This progress reflects ongoing administrative reforms aimed at modernizing public sector operations and enhancing institutional efficiency.

stories.title: Awami Raj Party Chief Iqrar-ul-Hassan Pleads Not Guilty in NCCIA Case
stories.summary:
A Judicial Magistrate in East Karachi formally indicted Awami Raj Party leader Iqrar-ul-Hassan on Friday in a legal case initiated by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency. During the court proceedings, the accused entered a plea of not guilty to the charges leveled against him.

The presiding magistrate instructed the prosecution to present its evidence and summoned prosecution witnesses to provide their testimonies during the upcoming hearing scheduled for December 9. Furthermore, the court instructed the defendant to guarantee his personal attendance on that specific date.

In a separate petition presented during the session, legal counsel for Iqrar-ul-Hassan requested the restoration of his mobile phone, which authorities confiscated at the time of his arrest. The court listened to the arguments surrounding this request and announced that its decision would be delivered on Monday, noting that the corresponding forensic report is anticipated by that time.

Separately in Lahore, the Punjab Revenue Authority issued a stern warning regarding strict measures against hotels and restaurants that obstruct the rollout of the provincial digital payment system. PRA Chairman Moazzam Iqbal Sappra led a recent meeting focused on advancing digital transactions, where officials addressed concerns regarding tax evasion and document forgery.

stories.title: SECP Mandates UDIN Verification for Company Audit Report Submissions
stories.summary:
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan has formally instructed companies to verify the Unique Document Identification Number on their auditor reports prior to submitting audited financial statements. This directive applies to all business entities mandated by existing legislation to file such documents with the commission.

A Unique Document Identification Number serves as a specific identifier that allows individuals to verify the authenticity of an audit report's issuer and prevents the circulation of fraudulent documentation. Qualified auditors generate these unique identifiers through online portals maintained by their respective professional bodies, namely the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan or the Institute of Cost and Management Accountants of Pakistan.

Under Regulation 6A of the Auditors Reporting Obligations Regulations from 2018, auditors are legally required to integrate a UDIN onto every official report they generate under these guidelines. Business organizations are expected to check the validity of this number via the appropriate institute portal before completing their regulatory submissions.

The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan stated it will only accept financial filings if the attached auditor report features a verified and authentic UDIN. Utilizing an unverified or invalid number may result in official regulatory intervention or formal civil and criminal legal proceedings under the prevailing laws.

stories.title: Pakistan Strongly Condemns Houthi Missile Strike on Riyadh Financial District
stories.summary:
Pakistan has formally condemned a suspected Houthi missile attack directed at King Abdullah Financial District in Riyadh, conveying strong support for Saudi Arabia and backing its fundamental right to defend its territory and sovereignty. The Foreign Office released a statement describing the strike as a serious breach of Saudi sovereignty, warning that persistent attacks on civilian infrastructure and economic centers endanger civilian lives and undermine regional stability.

The diplomatic statement emphasized that such aggressive actions must end immediately. Islamabad reaffirmed its close standing with the leadership and citizens of Saudi Arabia, emphasizing support for measures taken to safeguard residents and protect the nation's security, while reiterating its dedication to fostering lasting regional peace.

This condemnation followed a suspected missile strike hitting the PIF Tower, which serves as the headquarters for the sovereign wealth fund of Saudi Arabia. The impact shattered windows across multiple floors and inflicted structural damage to the metal exterior, marking the second incident in under two weeks to affect a prominent landmark in the capital's financial hub after an Aramco facility was hit on November 8.

Emergency responders and fire crews rushed to the scene while authorities restricted entry and cleared individuals from the area. While initial reports indicated no immediate casualties, the Saudi-led coalition monitoring the conflict confirmed it intercepted a projectile threat directed at Riyadh, noting that falling debris caused material damage.

stories.title: Mir Raza Ali JIT Seeks Bank Record Access and Witness Cooperation
stories.summary:
The Joint Investigation Team probing the homicide of Mir Raza Ali has approached a court for authorization to interrogate specific suspects and review relevant bank accounts. Sources indicate the team formally requested permission to examine the financial records of individuals including Ahmed Bhardey and Abdullah Bhardey, prompting the court to issue notices to the relevant parties.

Additionally, the investigators asked the court to compel pertinent banking institutions and organizations to fully cooperate with the ongoing inquiry. The application notes that the investigative body aims to finalize its inquiries and subsequently submit the final police report to the judicial authorities.

Meanwhile, attorney Jibran Nasir addressed a formal letter to the Sindh Home Minister to voice apprehension regarding delays in executing recommendations proposed by the judicial commission tied to the murder investigation. Nasir criticized the absence of certain members from Joint Investigation Team sessions and requested status updates on subcommittee decisions, noting a lack of communication regarding a one-member inquiry committee led by Zulfiqar Ali Lark.

Nasir urged formal departmental actions against responsible officials and highlighted that the parents of Mir Raza, who serve as vital witnesses, had not been summoned by the three-member investigative committee. In a separate development, the Punjab Revenue Authority warned Lahore hotels and restaurants against creating obstacles for the provincial digital payment infrastructure during a meeting chaired by PRA Chairman Moazzam Iqbal Sappra.

stories.title: Karachi Family Dispute Leaves Three Dead After Tragic Shooting
stories.summary:
A domestic dispute in the Landhi area of Karachi resulted in a fatal shooting on Friday morning. According to initial details, a local man opened fire and killed his wife and brother-in-law in Old Muzaffarabad Colony before turning the weapon on himself. Police and rescue personnel rushed to the scene to secure the location and initiate an official inquiry into the tragic event.

Following the shooting, authorities transferred the bodies of the deceased individuals to the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) for necessary medico-legal procedures. The incident occurred as investigators continue to look into separate domestic violence cases in the country, highlighting broader concerns regarding family conflicts and safety.

In an unrelated recent development, medical authorities released a detailed post-mortem report concerning 13-year-old domestic worker Fatima Asghar. The autopsy, conducted by the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), confirmed that the minor suffered severe physical torture before her death, sustaining roughly 20 fresh and old injuries spanning from her head to her feet.

The medical findings revealed extensive bruising, swelling, and blood clots in vital organs such as the heart and kidneys, with the official cause of death attributed to repeated physical assaults leading to cardiopulmonary arrest. The young victim had reportedly worked at the official residence of a senior Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) officer located in Islamabad's Police Lines Headquarters, prompting legal experts to urge a thorough examination of the circumstances surrounding her employment and abuse.

stories.title: Cricket Australia Captain Pat Cummins' Manager Defends Him Against Scandals
stories.summary:
The ongoing "Sandpapergate" controversy surrounding the 2018 ball-tampering incident has intensified following fresh claims regarding team-wide knowledge. Neil Maxwell, manager of Australia Test captain Pat Cummins, strongly criticized the intense scrutiny faced by the skipper, dismissing the criticism as unfounded hysteria that does not reflect reality.

The renewed controversy was sparked by retired player Usman Khawaja's autobiography, which alleged that the entire squad was aware of the plot during the Cape Town Test. These claims were subsequently supported by Cameron Bancroft, the player who used the sandpaper on the ball, who stated in a newspaper column that the whole team knew and expressed feelings of betrayal by the captain.

Despite the pressure and intense public scrutiny, Neil Maxwell defended Cummins' lengthy press conference and his eight-year stance, asserting that there is no serious case establishing the captain as an architect of ball-tampering.
